title: Historical Problem
description: Essential Criteria: Clearly state the need for a mechanism to prevent atoms from emitting light before Quantum Mechanics.

title: Quantum Explanation
description: Essential Criteria: Explain how Quantum Mechanics allows atoms in excited states to remain stable without emitting light.

title: Emission Mechanism
description: Essential Criteria: Describe the role of the single-photon creation operator in the emission of light from excited atoms.

title: Classical Electrodynamics
description: Important Criteria: Discuss the implications of classical electrodynamics on atomic stability and light emission.

title: Spontaneous Transition
description: Important Criteria: Mention the concept of spontaneous transition in excited states leading to light emission.

title: Common Misconceptions
description: Pitfall Criteria: Avoid stating that atoms in excited states do not emit light at all, as spontaneous emission occurs.

title: Units and Terminology
description: Optional Criteria: Use appropriate terminology related to quantum mechanics and atomic structure throughout the explanation.
